parsed.title: Discussion on taxes, domain purchase, and app feasibility

claims.text: User P1 paid 500 UAH to aunt Sveta to handle tax declaration issues and avoided larger penalties by re‑filing correctly.
The inspector ignored declarations for 1.5 years, later was reprimanded and started demanding re‑verification of all years.
Using Sveta’s help, the correct re‑submission cost about 1000 UAH, avoiding full fines.
Accurate tax calculation depends on correctly matching columns and numbers, not just the calculator itself.
P2 mentions not having bought a domain yet.
P4 doubts purchasing a domain, calling it a “sri” (useless) thing.
P1 suggests that buying a calculator (presumably tax calculator) would provide money for a domain.
P1 argues web platforms are less profitable than Android/iOS, have poor SEO, no external traffic, and low user retention due to paywalls.
P1 notes a successful podcast mentions fast delivery (< week) and cross‑platform stack (Flutter) by copying popular ideas.
P4 questions whether there are even ten people willing to pay 299 UAH for the product.
P1 asks if the source code can be found by searching for the password.
P4 jokes that they didn't pay 299 UAH for it.
P4 says the code is delivered in a bundle.
P4 claims the bundle contains the paid feature.
P4 describes the project as a “free vibe‑code” that will be inspected by those who know the password.
